hero.title: Patch, protect, and watch
hero.text: Keep the proven state from drifting: Windows updates by ring through SBD-WSUS01, a living inventory on SBD-MGMT01, managed protection through SBD-EPO01, and credentialed scans from SBD-NESSUS01, with Linux packages from SBD-REPO01 (course 1.8). Follow the build, explore the dependencies, and keep the evidence.

scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing SBD-WSUS01, SBD-MGMT01, SBD-EPO01 and SBD-NESSUS01 behind the core with SBD-REPO01 from course 1.8, SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 and the 50 Windows PCs in front, and the update, agent, package and scan paths each lesson adds.
scene.completeCaption: Windows systems take updates by ring from SBD-WSUS01 and check in with SBD-EPO01, SBD-MGMT01 keeps the living inventory, SBD-NESSUS01 installs only from SBD-REPO01 and scans each VLAN on the standing cadence.

nodes.name: SBD-WSUS01
nodes.title: SBD-WSUS01 · 10.0.20.30
nodes.description: The only road Windows updates travel. Content arrives on hashed media across the air gap, and approvals move ring by ring: pilot, broad, then the domain controllers and Tier 0 servers. Members check metadata over HTTPS 8531 and pull signed content over HTTP 8530.

nodes.name: SBD-REPO01
nodes.title: SBD-REPO01 · 10.0.70.20
nodes.description: Built in course 1.8: the one approved source for Linux packages. It serves a dated, signature-verified snapshot over HTTP on TCP 80 (F19). In this course SBD-NESSUS01 becomes its second consumer.

nodes.name: SBD-MGMT01
nodes.title: SBD-MGMT01 · 10.0.70.10
nodes.description: Keeps the living component inventory: every system with its OU, VLAN, address, ring, software sources, and scan status. Updates on every join and retirement, and a monthly reconciliation against the directory and the DHCP leases, keep it current.

nodes.name: SBD-EPO01
nodes.title: SBD-EPO01 · 10.0.50.30
nodes.description: The single Trellix ePO server that manages endpoint protection and DLP policy. Agents, deployed ring by ring, start their check-ins on TCP 443, and its threat events forward into the logging pipeline of courses 1.9–1.11.

nodes.name: SBD-NESSUS01
nodes.title: SBD-NESSUS01 · 10.0.50.20
nodes.description: Domain-joined Linux scanner that runs credentialed scans VLAN by VLAN: SMB 445 and WMI to Windows, SSH 22 to Linux. Its reach is the course’s one deliberate wide permit, and the domain controller scan account is a Tier 0 credential.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 · 10.0.60.20
nodes.description: The server administration seat from course 1.7. Pilot and broad-ring approvals are Tier 1 work from here, as is administration of member servers such as SBD-MGMT01. Critical-ring approvals and domain controller agent policy stay on AdminJumpBox01 with Tier 0 accounts.

nodes.name: 50 Windows PCs
nodes.title: 50 Windows PCs · 10.0.80.100–199
nodes.description: The course 1.12 fleet on VLAN 80: its sample machines sit in the pilot ring and the rest in the broad ring. Each PC takes updates from SBD-WSUS01, runs an agent that checks in with SBD-EPO01, and lets the scanner through its host firewall for SMB 445 and WMI.

stepTitles: Define the three update rings and their order
Write the one-approved-source rule
Decide the air-gap feeding cadence
Add the course’s register rows
design.mistake: Putting the domain controllers in the first ring because they matter most. A bad update would then land on the identity fabric first; the critical ring goes last and installs only what the pilot and broad rings already survived.
design.network: Four systems are planned: SBD-WSUS01 on VLAN 20, SBD-EPO01 and SBD-NESSUS01 on VLAN 50, and SBD-MGMT01 on VLAN 70 beside SBD-REPO01, which already serves Linux packages from course 1.8. The fleet and SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 run from earlier courses; no new paths are shown until each service is built.

control.name: Configuration Change Control
control.body: Rings make every update a controlled change: it is tested on the pilot ring, approved for the next ring only after it survives, and recorded at each step. Writing the order down before the first update arrives makes the process reviewable.
control.question: Which systems could the network lose for a day without harm, and does your ring table put them first?

checklist: I assigned every system to the pilot, broad, or critical ring and wrote down the order.
I wrote the one-source rule for Windows updates, Linux packages, and protection definitions, and how exceptions are documented.
I recorded the feeding cadence beside course 1.8's snapshot cadence and added the WSUS, ePO agent, and scanner rows to the register with owners, confirming F19 covers SBD-NESSUS01.

stepTitles: Install WSUS and scope its products and classifications
Import update content through the offline process
Create ring groups and link the ring GPOs
Approve the first cycle and promote it ring by ring
wsus.mistake: Approving the first update cycle for every computer group at once. The domain controllers and Tier 0 servers then install something no ring has proven; approve for the pilot ring only, and promote once it has installed and reported.
wsus.network: SBD-WSUS01 is live on VLAN 20. The fleet checks metadata over HTTPS 8531 and pulls signed content over HTTP 8530, and SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 approves the pilot and broad rings. Update content arrives by hand on approved media, with no network path across the air gap.

control.name: Flaw Remediation
control.body: WSUS is the flaw-remediation channel: updates are tested on the pilot ring before they reach later rings, and the per-ring approval and install timeline records when each system received them.
control.question: How long should an approval stay in the pilot ring before it moves on, and what would make you stop it?

checklist: I recorded the product and classification scope and the hashes of the offline import.
I confirmed with gpresult that each ring’s GPO applies and that every system reports to its ring’s group.
I recorded the first cycle’s approval and install times for each ring, in the written order.

stepTitles: Build SBD-MGMT01 in the Servers OU
Load every system into the component inventory
Define update-on-change and monthly reconciliation
Name the owner and file the first reconciliation
mgmt.mistake: Building the inventory once and treating it as finished. Without joins and retirements updating it and a monthly comparison against the directory and DHCP leases, it drifts back into a snapshot, and the coverage claims in lessons 4 and 5 lose their denominator.
mgmt.network: SBD-MGMT01 joins SBD-REPO01 on VLAN 70 and is administered from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 on VLAN 60. The inventory it holds is the list that lessons 4 and 5 measure protection and scan coverage against.

control.name: System Component Inventory
control.body: This lesson builds the component inventory itself: every system with its attributes, a named owner, and a reconciliation that shows the record still matches the directory and the leases.
control.question: If the inventory, the directory, and the DHCP leases disagreed, which would you trust first, and why?

checklist: I loaded every modeled system with its OU, VLAN, address, ring, software sources, and scan status.
I compared the directory and DHCP lease counts with the inventory and recorded any mismatches as findings.
I wrote down the inventory’s owner, its update-on-change rule, and its monthly reconciliation cadence.

stepTitles: Build SBD-EPO01 with no listeners on the endpoints
Deploy agents ring by ring
Apply the protection and DLP policy baseline
Verify coverage and trace a test detection
epo.mistake: Leaving the agent’s peer-to-peer and RelayServer features on. Every endpoint then opens listeners for the server (TCP 8081, UDP 8082) that no register row allows; with them off, the agent starts each connection on TCP 443 and endpoints open no listener.
epo.network: SBD-EPO01 is live on VLAN 50. Agents on the fleet start their check-ins on TCP 443, the fleet keeps its WSUS path, and the console stays reachable only from the administration plane on VLAN 60.

control.name: Malicious Code Protection
control.body: Managed agents give every endpoint the same protection policy from one console, with definitions fed on the written offline cadence. Coverage reconciled against the inventory and a traced test detection show the mechanism works, not just that it was installed.
control.question: If an endpoint stopped checking in, how soon would you know, and which record would show it?

checklist: I compared the agents checking in with the living inventory and recorded every gap.
I recorded each policy baseline setting, including on-access protection, the scan schedule, and the DLP scope, as a decision.
I traced a standard test file’s detection from the endpoint to the console and into the analyst’s search.

stepTitles: Build SBD-NESSUS01 on REPO01 packages with scoped scan accounts
Run the first credentialed scan and triage it
Wire results into the pipeline, records, and cadence
Baseline this course’s systems and hand off
nessus.mistake: Using one scan account for every target. The domain controller scan credential is Tier 0; reusing it on member servers or the fleet exposes it to lower tiers. Keep it apart from the member-server account and use it only for DC scan jobs.
nessus.network: SBD-NESSUS01 is live on VLAN 50 and scans across the VLANs, shown here reaching the fleet over SMB 445 and WMI. It installs packages only from SBD-REPO01 with the course 1.8 client configuration, and the fleet keeps its WSUS and ePO paths.

control.name: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
control.body: Scheduled credentialed scans, plus scans triggered by change, make vulnerability scanning routine rather than an event. Classifying every finding as fixed, a documented deviation, or a POA&M candidate keeps the results usable.
control.question: What evidence shows a finding was fixed, rather than simply no longer reported?

checklist: I kept the scan accounts separate, used the domain controller account only for DC scan jobs, and confirmed their use is logged.
I classified every finding from the first credentialed scan as fix-now, a documented deviation, or a POA&M candidate.
I filed baselines for this course’s four systems, SBD-REPO01’s scheduled rescan, and rescans of the systems whose agents or policies changed.
